page: The Microsoft Azure FX32-16mds_v2 is a specialized instance designed for compute-heavy workloads that require high clock speeds alongside substantial memory density. Hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading. The CPU includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Hardware resources include 672 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to 42 GB per vCPU, bundled with 1,890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without a discrete GPU.

Benchmark data reflects the high-frequency design of the platform. Single-core performance is in the top tier, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 2,315 and high single-threaded text processing results. Data decompression and compression routines also place in the upper quartile, with gzip compression reaching 34.78 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 14.22 GB/sec. Large block memory write bandwidth measures 91.91 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Multi-core throughput across stress-ng and PassMark reflects middle-tier rankings, aligning with the constrained 16-vCPU physical topology.

From an architectural standpoint, the FX32-16mds_v2 provides a targeted resource balance. Limiting compute allocation to 16 vCPUs while providing an expansive 672 GB memory footprint reduces core-based software licensing costs while satisfying extreme working set demands. Bundled NVMe storage supports low-latency local scratch operations. The instance is well suited for electronic design automation (EDA), large-scale relational and in-memory databases, financial risk simulations, and compilation pipelines requiring substantial memory per thread.
description: The Microsoft Azure FX32-16mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-dense virtual machine built for compute tasks requiring massive memory capacity per core. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, it supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 260 MB of L3 cache, backed by 672 GB of RAM and 1,890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX, but does not include GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-core Geekbench performance alongside strong memory write bandwidth and decompression speeds, while multi-core metrics sit in the middle quartile due to its constrained 16-thread profile. By delivering 42 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance optimizes licensing costs for core-bound enterprise software. It fits electronic design automation (EDA), relational and in-memory database operations, batch compression pipelines, and memory-intensive simulation workloads.
